quote: 1. The first thing I heard when I got in the business was bulls make money, bears make money, and pigs get slaughtered. I'm here to tell you I was a pig. And I strongly believe the only way to make long-term returns in our business that are superior is by being a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 2. My goal is not to buy at the lowest or cheapest price but at the "right" price, just as a stock is ready to move significantly higher. Trying to pick a bottom is unnecessary and a waste of time; it misses the whole point.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 3. You must have a love for the market in order to be successful in this game. Really, a huge interest.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 4. When you truly commit to something, you have no alternative but success.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 5. Virtually every superperformance phase in big, winning stocks occurred while the stock price was in a definite price uptrend. In almost every case, the trend was identifiable early in the superperformance advance.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 6. Don't ever feel that you are very good. The second you do, you are dead.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 7. If you're early on in your career and they give you a choice between a great mentor or higher pay, take the mentor every time. It's not even close. And don't even think about leaving that mentor until your learning curve peaks.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 8. Those who trade without a stop eventually stop trading.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 9. The maximum loss I allow is 7 percent, and usually I am out of a losing stock a lot quicker.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 10. I never try to make money in the stock market. I buy on the assumption that they could close the market the next day and not reopen it for five years.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 11. Trading without a stop-loss is like driving a car without brakes.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 12. To compound your money, and not your mistakes, your goal is to buy on the way up—not on the way down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 13. Concentrating your bets decreases your overall risk because where you tend to be in trouble is if you have 35 or 40 names. If you have a big massive position, it has your attention.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 14. Investing styles may differ among successful market players, but without exception, winning stock traders share certain key traits required for success. Fall short in those qualities and you will surely part ways with your money.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 15. The single most important advice I can give anybody is: Learn from your mistakes. That is the only way to become a successful trader.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 16. I like putting all my eggs in one basket and then watching the basket very carefully.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 17. Calculating risks shrewdly is the main ingredient for consistent superior performance. Pros play percentage ball, and that's why, in the long run, they are more consistent than amateurs.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 18. Every time I buy a stock, I write down the reasons why I bought it. Doing this helps cement in my mind the characteristics of a winning stock. Maybe even more important, it helps me learn from my mistakes.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 19. When you sell half, if the stock goes higher you say to yourself, 'Thank goodness I kept half.' If the stock goes lower, you'll say, 'Thank goodness I sold half.' Psychologically, it's a win/win either way.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 20. You need to be decisive, open-minded, flexible and competitive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 21. I put a lot more weight into how this stock is acting relative to the S&P — you can see real divergences when stocks are making new highs and the relative strength line is not.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 22. Don't bet big unless a) you love your thesis, and b) you're hot.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 23. There really is no intelligent reason to increase your trading size if your positions are showing losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 24. The higher the relative strength the better. Once the relative strength starts falling off, I usually get out of the stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 25. I think contrarianism is overrated. Soros used to say the crowd's right 80% of the time. You just can't be caught in the other 20% because you can get your head handed to you. I get some intellectual satisfaction out of playing in the 20%, but as a concept, I think contrarianism is overrated.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 26. Ideally, I like to concentrate my capital in the best names, for example, devoting 20 to 25 percent of my portfolio in each of my top four or five stock picks.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 27. If I get stopped out, I get stopped out. I don't think, I just get out.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 28. When you tell yourself, I'm going to break my rule just this once, you open the door to losing discipline, because it's never just 'one time.'
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 29. I think a lot of my performance has been because I'm flexible in terms of the assets I use. I'm not afraid to just play in bonds or currencies or this or that.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 30. All the stocks we buy have some institutional sponsorship because mutual funds have such buying power that when they really like a company, they keep on buying it, and it keeps on going.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 31. I studied historical models of great winning stocks to ingrain in my mind what a stock looked like before it made a major move. I tried to get to the point where I was looking at the exact same things O'Neil did. He was my role model.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 32. You can get so focused on the results that you don't do what you should be doing.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 33. I always try to keep losses very small. 7 per cent is a great percentage to use.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 34. In the stock market, you can make money or you can make excuses, but you can't make both. Do whatever it takes to eliminate your own personal excuses. Your road to success starts by taking responsibility.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 35. Never stray from the basics of rule number one of always going in with a plan.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 36. The market keeps teaching the same lesson to every serious practitioner who is willing to listen.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 37. One of the reasons of my success was open mindedness to various asset classes. It gives you the discipline to not play when you shouldn't be playing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 38. You must not risk more than you can reasonably expect to gain; otherwise, you're stacking the odds against you, and that's gambling.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 39. I went from mediocre to a stellar performer when I told myself: To heck with worrying about the money and obsessing over the scoreboard. I'm just going to focus on being the best trader I can be and sticking to the rules. Then the money followed.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 40. If you try to learn from every single trade that you make, you are only going to get better and better as time goes on.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 41. If you find yourself getting stopped out of your positions over and over, there can only be two things wrong: 1. Your stock selection criteria are flawed. 2. The general market environment is hostile.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 42. It's not enough to have knowledge, a dream, or passion; it's what you do with what you know that counts. The best time to get started is now!
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 43. I've also never hung onto a security if the reason I bought it has changed.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 44. What you have to look at is what people think it's going to earn. If you can see something in two years is going to be entirely different than the conventional wisdom, that's how you make money.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 45. My goal is just to become a better and better trader, more and more disciplined, so I can be more and more successful in the market. I am disciplined in implementing the system and sticking to it.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 46. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 47. If you want to make money in the market, if you want to be successful in anything, you really got to put in a lot of time.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 48. My longevity stems from the fact that I try to control risk as much as possible. When the market starts down I sell quickly and don't let the losses get out of hand.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 49. I'm always thinking about losing money as opposed to making money. Don't focus on making money, focus on protecting what you have.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 50. I believe the best way to manage risk is to be bullish when you have a compelling risk/reward and bearish when you don't.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 51. The market is the greatest humbling device in the world.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 52. Unrequited love in the stock market can be very expensive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 53. A loss never bothers me after I take it. I might be wrong on a stock more than once in a row, but I'm not going to be wrong for very long.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 54. You want to be involved in a stock while it is undergoing accumulation, not distribution.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 55. You should not risk more than you expect to gain on average; I call that the 'Cardinal Sin.'
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 56. If you normally cut losses at 7 to 8 percent, cut them at 5 to 6 percent.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 57. My percentage of winners is only about 50/50, because I cut my losers very quickly.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 58. With each buy order I enter, I know the exact price where I am going to sell at a loss if things don't work out as expected. I define this price level before I get in.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 59. Everyone makes mistakes; that's unavoidable. But not correcting a mistake or minimizing the damage of a position gone wrong is completely under your own control. The big mistakes start out as small mistakes that were allowed to get out of hand. You must realize that big losses are a choice and take responsibility for controlling them.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 60. If it reenters its base, I have a rule to cut at least 50 percent of the position.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 61. I'm only rich because I know when I'm wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 62. Growth comes at the expense of comfort.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 63. There is a lot more noise and movement in the market with high speed trading and computerized algorithms, but the stocks that have the biggest moves continue to have the same characteristics.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 64. I've never made a buy at a low that I didn't just feel terrible and scared to death making it. It's easy to sell at the bottom. You can go home that night and it relieves you of your nerves.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 65. It's better to lose correctly than to win incorrectly.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 66. I usually hold my big winners for about six to twelve months, stocks that aren't that strong about three months, and my losers less than two weeks.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 67. Hope is not a strategy.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 68. Those who succeed big at anything all have the same attitude: You keep going until it happens or you die trying. Quitting is not an option.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 69. Expectancy is your percentage of winning trades multiplied by your average gain, divided by your percentage of losing trades multiplied by your average loss. Maintain a positive expectancy, and you're a winner.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 70. The biggest mistake investors make is they invest in the present rather than forward looking and looking at where the puck is going instead of where the puck is.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 71. You want to get on board when institutional money is pouring into a stock and lifting it significantly higher.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 72. Figuring yourself out and developing a discipline are probably the most important things.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 73. I've learned many things from George Soros, but perhaps the most significant is that it's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 74. It's like studying an animal; certain stocks have certain characteristics and a certain way of behaving. You need to recognize when those characteristics are changing and act accordingly.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 75. What I learned from George Soros was sizing is 70 or 80 percent of the equation.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 76. Earnings don't move the overall market; it's the Federal Reserve Board... focus on the central banks, and focus on the movement of liquidity... most people in the market are looking for earnings and conventional measures. It's liquidity that moves markets.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 77. If you want to mitigate risk effectively, you simply must acknowledge that stocks don't manage themselves. You're the manager, and it's up to you to protect your hard-earned capital.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 78. There's nothing new under the sun... things just repeat themselves over and over again. It's really identifying what has existed and what has happened in the past.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 79. If you look at what the Fed did, the radical gamble they took to get inflation up 30 basis points from 1.7 to 2, it's, to me, sort of a risk-reward bet. You bet 1 to lose 40? And they lost.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 80. This is the biggest redistribution of wealth from the middle class and the poor to the rich ever.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 81. The key is to see things as they are—operating in the now—without seeing things as worse than they are out of fear, or better than they are out of greed.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 82. I don't really like hedging. To me, if something needs to be hedged, you shouldn't have a position in it.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 83. The road to success in the stock market is not a system or strategy; it's within you, and it will be realized only to the extent that you are able to control and direct your emotions as you encounter challenges.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 84. I make my money on the few stocks a year that double and triple in price. The profits in those trades easily makes up for all the small losers.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 85. Traders have to take their ego and throw it in a trash can when walking into the trading day because they are going to be wrong.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 86. If you want to reap big gains in the market, make up your mind right now that you are going to separate trading from your ego. It's more important to make money than it is to be right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 87. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 88. Bad news is sometimes the best buying opportunity life gives you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 89. Amateurs think about how much money they can make. Professionals think about how much money they could lose.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 90. Trade what you see, not what you think.
speaker: Mark Minervini
